To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Sort-Merge feature-selection method can be applied to a wide range of video retrieval tasks, including the simultaneous detection and refinement of video segment boundaries, and that the resulting feature hierarchy can be used to efficiently implement video retrieval systems with real-time lazy evaluation.

(1) Sort-Merge feature induction can be applied to any feature set to construct an efficient hierarchical index for video retrieval; (2) the index can be used to simultaneously segment and categorize video in a coarse-finer manner; and (3) the index can also be used for fast video retrieval by lazy evaluation.

(i) Sort-Merge feature induction is a new heuristic method for machine learning, and that it can be applied in the domain of fast video indexing, (ii) Sort-Merge can be used in combination with Fastmap for dimension reduction and Mahalanabois distance for likelihood determination, (iii) Sort-Merge is a new method for fast video indexing and retrieval, and (iv) Sort-Merge enables fast video indexing by the approach of coarse-fine segmentation and lazy evaluation
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and implementation of a fast and effective video retrieval system that is based on a new feature selection algorithm and the novel combination of video segment detection and categorization, and query-based lazy evaluation.
the design of fast, accurate, and flexible video retrieval methods that can be easily adapted to different applications.
the design and implementation of a fast and effective retrieval system for video segments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system can achieve a fast retrieval of video segments by a combination of machine learning methods and the approach of lazy evaluations.

we present a new approach to the problem of video retrieval that is based on a novel feature selection method that exploits machine learning techniques, a new method for simultaneous segmentation and classification, and an approach to efficient query evaluation.
our system is able to achieve fast and accurate retrieval of video segments by a novel combination of feature selection, lazy evaluation, and boundary refinement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our methods can be easily integrated in any existing video indexing system to improve its performance and efficiency.
the proposed system can achieve high accuracy and fast speed simultaneously, which is a significant advantage over the existing systems that have high accuracy or fast speed but not both.

our video retrieval system is capable of retrieving the desired video segments in a few seconds, with an average accuracy of 90%, and with a precision-recall trade-off curve that can be adjusted to user preference.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Sort-Merge method can induce small feature sets that are more accurate than those induced by the state of the art, and that the resulting feature set hierarchy can be used in the context of video segment retrieval to improve the efficiency of the indexing and query processes.
the combination of these methods can enable fast and efficient video retrieval systems that are robust to the problem of noisy training examples.
machine learning techniques can be applied to video retrieval to achieve high accuracy and efficiency.
